## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Treatment
where: TreatmentService (uses), src/business/treatmentService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
return this.treatments.create({ hiveId, productId: found.id, startDate: start, endDate: end });
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are two different concepts. A Treatment is a single event where a product is applied to a hive over a period of time. In TreatmentService, a treatment is created with its own fields: `this.treatments.create({ hiveId, productId: found.id, startDate: start, endDate: end })`. It points to a product through `productId` but is not the product. A Treatment Product is a catalog entry for the product itself. It is stored separately in TreatmentProductRepository as `private readonly items = new Map<string, TreatmentProductRecord>();`. The graph also shows two separate repositories: TreatmentService calls both TreatmentRepository.create and TreatmentProductRepository.create/findByName. So the link between them is a reference from one to the other (many treatments to one product), not the same thing under two names.
